source.title: What does a deep neural network confidently perceive? The effective dimension of high certainty class manifolds and their low confidence boundaries
source.authors: Stanislav Fort; E. Cubuk; S. Ganguli; S. Schoenholz

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains networks on randomly reshuffled labels and reports training accuracy, while its main measurement is class-manifold dimension rather than the original studies’ generalization and optimization measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for fitting random labels, but does not rely on that citation alone: it reports its own random-label training setup and says the ResNet20v1 models reach 100% training accuracy. The class-manifold dimension results are measurements of a related geometric property, not direct tests of the listed claim versions; recorded under fits_no_version. No results for V2–V6.
record.test_reason: Figure 14 reports the study's own ResNet20v1 models achieving 100% training accuracy on randomly permuted CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 labels. This uses the original claim's training-and-accuracy method; the paper's separate geometry measurements do not change that classification. Appendix A.1 specifies SGD with momentum and L2 regularization, bearing also on the weight-decay component of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's random-label conclusion is accurate: random-label training yields smaller effective class manifolds despite perfect training accuracy. The authors associate this with failure to generalize, without establishing causation. More broadly, they report an association between larger class manifolds and better performance and robustness, with ensembling as an exception.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses standard supervised training with randomly reshuffled labels, but its central method measures class-manifold geometry rather than directly reproducing the original studies’ fit, test-error, and training-time measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100) changes the measured class-manifold dimension; the text does not give a numerical comparison in prose.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label ResNet20v1 models have higher critical cutting-plane dimensions and lower effective class-manifold dimensions than models trained on meaningful labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly permuted CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 labels produce lower-dimensional high-confidence class manifolds than meaningful labels in ResNet20v1.

record.code_released: https://github.com/ (the text says the code is on Github but gives no repository URL)
record.problems: Test error for the random-label models is described only as failure to generalize, with no numerical result. The paper does not state whether the random-label experiment kept architecture and training hyperparameters unchanged. Random-label geometry comparisons are primarily shown in figures; the text gives no numerical d*50% comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported per-class values were extracted from Figures 6 and 14; the text gives aggregate qualitative comparisons and the captions identify the class-wise plots.

untested.parts: Numerical chance-level test error is not reported. Section 4.4 states failure to generalize. Appendix A.1 supplies a common architecture and training recipe, but an explicit matched-hyperparameter comparison between real-label and random-label runs is absent.
Relative training time and convergence as a function of label corruption are not measured.
Training to fit shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs is not tested. Test-time Gaussian corruption is a different experiment.
No sweep over intermediate label-noise fractions or corresponding training and test errors is reported.

Dropout and augmentation preventing random-label fitting are not tested. Neither is generalization on true labels after removing explicit regularization. The weight-decay evidence uses the general recipe in Appendix A.1 without a separate regularization ablation.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noise is not measured. Evolution of class-manifold dimension does not establish that order.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the general optimization and regularization details in Appendix A.1. No incomplete or failed fitting result warrants limits_scope or challenges. The geometric distinction between real and random labels alone does not test V6's learning-order claim.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance and whether architecture or training hyperparameters were unchanged are not directly reported for the random-label models.

rows.value: d*50% rises significantly; class-manifold dimension is lower than for semantically meaningful labels.
rows.note: This is the paper’s geometry result, not a measure named by V1–V6.
rows.check: The geometric difference is reported, but class-manifold dimension cannot establish any listed version's effect. Retain this finding under fits_no_version rather than interpreting its observed geometry as an observed claim effect.
